messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: modelling positive transformed data?
parts:
Hopefully a quick'un!

Let's say I have postive data y and I want to express a model whereby these are the result of some latent gaussian z where z ~ normal(mu,sigma) and y = abs(z). How would I code this in Stan? 

Here's my first go at this:

  data{
    int nY ;
    vector[nY] y ;
  }
  parameters{
    real zMean ;
    real<lower=0> zSd ;
    vector[nY] z ;
  }
  model{
    zMean ~ normal(0,1) ;
    zSd ~ weibull(2,1) ;
    z ~ normal(zMean,zSd) ;
    y ~ normal(fabs(z),0.00001);
  }

But I'm pretty sure this isn't the proper way to do it. Any thoughts?

Mike

--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

~ Certainty is (possibly) folly ~

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] modelling positive transformed data?
parts:
Abs is a bad idea here — it makes the posterior multimodal.
Much easier to just log the data, either before you call Stan
or in the transformed data blog, and modeling log(y) with a
latent normal.  Of course in this case that’s just equivalent 
to modeling y with a log normal.

I don’t think this needs to be elaborated much, but a 0.00001
standard deviation is a terrible idea.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] modelling positive transformed data?
parts:
Ah! I think a mixture approach might actually apply here, as in:

  data{
    int nY ;
    vector<lower=0>[nY] y ;
  }
  parameters{
    real<lower=0> yMean ;
    real<lower=0> ySd ;
  }
  model{
    yMean ~ normal(0,1) ;
    ySd ~ weibull(2,1) ;
    target += log_mix(
      normal_cdf(0,yMean,ySd)
      , normal_lpdf(y|-yMean,ySd)
      , normal_lpdf(y|yMean,ySd)
    ) ;
  }

But alas when I try with some fake data I don't recover mean & sd, it just sticks with the sample mean & sd:

  library(rstan)
  set.seed(1)
  m = 1
  s = 1
  pnorm(0,m,s)
  #[1] 0.1586553  
  y = abs(rnorm(1e3,1,1))
  mean(y)
  #[1] 1.178634
  sd(y)
  #[1] 0.811356
  hist(y,br=100)
  post = rstan::stan(
    file = 'mix.stan'
